title: Caramel Apple Fair Cupcakes
shortDescription: Spiced apple cupcakes with a caramel swirl drizzle, ready in about 45 minutes total.
description: These cupcakes taste like a warm apple pie from the county fair, baked into a soft cake. I grated fresh apples right into the batter so every bite stays moist. A swirl of caramel goes into the batter before baking, then more caramel gets drizzled on top after frosting. It gives you that gooey caramel apple bite in every cupcake. I tested this recipe three times in my home kitchen to get the apple to cake ratio right. Too much apple made the cupcakes sink, so I found the sweet spot below Serve these at a fall party or after a school pickup. They hold up well at room temperature for a few hours, which makes them easy for parties.
ingredients: 1 cup peeled and finely grated apple (about 1 medium apple), squeezed lightly to remove extra juice
1/2 cup store bought soft caramel sauce, divided
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
1/2 tsp sea salt flakes, for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat softened butter and brown sugar together for 2 minutes until fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Mix in vanilla.
Add the flour mix in three parts, alternating with buttermilk. Mix just until combined.
Fold in the grated apple by hand. Do not overmix the batter.
Fill liners two thirds full. Drop 1/2 teaspoon of caramel sauce into the center of each cupcake and swirl gently with a toothpick.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Beat 1 cup butter until smooth. Add powdered sugar and cream, then beat 3 minutes until light and fluffy.
Pipe frosting on cooled cupcakes. Drizzle with remaining caramel sauce and finish with a pinch of sea salt flakes.
tips: Squeeze the grated apple in a paper towel before mixing it in. Extra juice makes the cake soggy.
Use a firm baking apple like Honeycrisp or Granny Smith. Soft apples turn mushy in the batter.
Warm the caramel sauce for a few seconds before drizzling so it pours smoothly.
Chill piped cupcakes for 10 minutes before drizzling caramel so the frosting holds its shape.

faq.question: Can I use apple sauce instead of grated apple?
faq.answer: Grated apple works better here. Apple sauce adds too much moisture and the cake can sink in the middle.

faq.question: Why did the caramel sink to the bottom of my cupcakes?
faq.answer: This happens if the caramel sauce is too thin or added in a large amount. Use a small 1/2 teaspoon swirl, not a full spoonful.

faq.question: Can I make these ahead for a fall party?
faq.answer: Yes. Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost and drizzle the day you serve them.

faq.question: What caramel sauce works best for the drizzle?
faq.answer: A thick, store bought soft caramel sauce holds its shape on top of frosting. Very runny caramel sauce will slide right off.

conclusion: These caramel apple cupcakes bring fair season flavor right to your kitchen. Grated apple keeps the cake moist, and the caramel swirl inside and out makes each bite feel special. Bake a batch this weekend and see why it is one of my favorite fall recipes.
